candidates.decision_relevance: Would distinguish transient top-100 proxy moves from persistent, representative participation broadening or narrowing when separating rotation from distribution.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly identify point-in-time top-100 breadth as proxy-only, with changing membership and no canonical broad-alt or large-cap breadth history.
candidates.metric_name: Membership-stable broad-alt and large-cap breadth series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Only changing-membership proxy snapshots are supplied, so persistence, cross-sectional participation, and lead-lag relative to price cannot be audited.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would resolve whether flow, depth, funding, open interest, liquidations, breadth, sentiment, and price weakness occurred in a consistent sequence or were coincident snapshots.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily and weekly reviews repeatedly report unavailable 1-hour anchors, zero-span 4-hour windows, non-exact 12/24-hour spans, and unknown timestamp order.
candidates.metric_name: Aligned hourly BTC/ETH price, flow, depth, funding, open-interest, breadth, sentiment, and liquidation history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Cross-horizon disagreement and missing event ordering prevent lead-lag analysis and leave transient shocks indistinguishable from persistent deterioration.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would distinguish long liquidation, short covering, forced selling, and leverage reset, materially improving interpretation of deleveraging and pullback evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Reviews state that liquidation aggregates are lower bounds with unverified completeness and do not identify liquidation composition; open-interest changes are directionally ambiguous.
candidates.metric_name: Venue-covered liquidation events with side, size, timestamp, and contemporaneous open-interest change
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregate lower-bound liquidation totals cannot show whether stress was long-driven, short-driven, complete, or followed by recovery.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would test whether settled ETF demand persisted, was concentrated, and translated into price and participation support during the disputed transition.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews cite positive settled ETF totals but repeatedly note stale coverage, absent prior-session comparisons, and no current flow-change sequence.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC/ETH ETF net-flow history with fund-level detail
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single or stale totals cannot establish persistence, concentration, within-period sequencing, or whether flows offset breadth and liquidity deterioration.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would provide contemporaneous macro context for distinguishing crypto-specific pullbacks from broader liquidity or risk-appetite shocks.
candidates.evidence_reference: Several daily outputs explicitly report macro fields as stale, absent, or unavailable and state that no current macro delta can be inferred.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamp-aligned macro and liquidity observations used by the existing research context
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses cannot determine whether crypto weakness or rotation occurred alongside a changing macro/liquidity backdrop, reducing attribution of the observed move.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would permit ex-ante audit of forecast quality and prevent completed-week observations from being mistaken for prospective evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews report that candidate specifications, freeze times, evidence cutoffs, confidence values, and matured outcomes are absent despite prior candidate counts.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen forecast candidate and outcome audit trail
candidates.missing_history_problem: Without immutable issue timestamps, available-information cutoffs, exact horizons/ranges, and later realized values, hindsight leakage, containment quality, calibration, and false-positive/false-negative costs cannot be scored.
